transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
- Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
The Department of Justice filed charges today
against former FBI Director James Comey for the third time.
Comey is charged with two counts,
including illegally sharing sensitive information.
He's drawn the ire of President Trump
since he led the 2016 Russia investigation
over alleged election interference.
A DOJ prosecution against Comey, of accusing Comey,
of threatening Trump in a photo of seashells
posted on social media is still pending.
Meanwhile, a New York federal judge has ordered
the Justice Department to reinstate Comey's daughter,
former prosecutor Maureen Comey, who was fired last year,
and Paris-Nate Perez reports.
- The ruling calls for Maureen Comey to receive back pay,
dating to when she was fired last year,
and for her to return as a prosecutor
to the Southern District of New York if she chooses.
Judge Jesse Furman wrote in the opinion
that the Department of Justice
invented a new and expansive theory of executive power
and violated her constitutional right to due process.
The Department never gave a performance-based reason
for her dismissal.
In a lawsuit last month, Maureen Comey alleged
that the real reason she was fired
was because her father is James Comey,
the former FBI Director who drew President Trump's ire.
In an emailed statement, the Justice Department
said it would appeal the decision.
Nate Perez, NPR News.
- The midterms are just over a week away
and millions of people have already voted,
and Paris Tamara Keith checks in
on the mid-decade redistricting effort
that was supposed to help Republicans.
- President Trump and his political team
pressured Republican-led states
to redraw congressional district lines,
and they were able to shift 15 districts nationwide
to favor the party's candidates.
But now, only a third of those districts
look like a sure thing for Republicans,
Nathan Gonzalez's editor of Inside Elections.
- Redistricting was supposed to be a firewall
for Republicans in this midterm election,
and it has just not turned out that way.
- Instead, the redrawn districts include
some of the most competitive
and expensive House races in the country.
Tamara Keith, NPR News.
- AI giant, Anthropic, the maker of clawed AI,
has filed paperwork for an initial public offering.
Analysts expect the listing to be one of the biggest
on record, NPR's John Ruich reports.
- Anthropic got its start just five years ago
when a group of senior researchers at OpenAI
led by Dario Amadeh broke away.
They were concerned that the company was not on a path
to develop AI safely.
Anthropic has since become a juggernaut,
and OpenAI's biggest competitor
was some of the most widely used AI models on the market.
Amadeh, now CEO, has issued some of the AI world's
sharpest warnings about the possibility
of AI spiraling out of human control.
The IPO perspective showed skyrocketing growth
at the company, and analysts say the IPO
could value the firm at 1.5 to two trillion dollars.
John Ruich, NPR News.
- The S&P 500 rose 7/10 of a percent today.
Later this week, earnings reports will come
from roughly one out of every three stocks in the S&P.
It's NPR.
France's government is pledging to replace
its national online university admissions platform in 2028
after weeks of mass protests over education
and living costs.
Higher Education Minister Philippe Baptiste announced
during a news conference substantial change for 2027
before the platform's replacement in 2028,
students have criticized unclear selection criteria
and unequal access to their preferred courses.
In Maryland and Virginia, school cafeterias
are serving blue catfish.
As NPR's Bill Chappell reports,
the fish is invasive and delicious.
- Blue catfish prey on young fish and blue crabs
that are the cornerstone of the economy
around the Chesapeake Bay.
Officials say if more people eat the fish,
it'll be easier to keep their numbers in check.
And some school districts are helping.
Beth Brewster oversees school food services
in Caroline County, Maryland.
She says when kids try it, catfish is off in a hit.
- One mom texted me.
Her son came home and was like, "Mom, mom."
They had breaded blue catfish with fries.
It was like the best day ever.
- Blue catfish were added to a couple rivers
near the Chesapeake Bay decades ago.
Wildlife managers thought they'd make a good trophy fish,
which they did, and that they'd stay in fresh water
away from crabs and other fisheries, but they didn't.
Now they're in every major tidal river and the bay itself.
Bill Chappell, NPR News.
- Tonight is the sports equinox.
Five pro-American leagues are playing at the same time.
Baseball's World Series, Monday Night Football,
the NBA, WNBA, and NHL all have games.
I'm Rylan Barton, this is NPR News from Washington.
This election season, let the NPR Politics podcast
save your time and your sanity.
We'll help you understand key races,
which polls you can safely ignore,
and what might happen if power shifts in Congress.
Our short daily episodes come out every afternoon
so you can spend less time
scrolling through each chaotic news cycle.
Make NPR Politics your hub for midterm election coverage,
follow our podcast on the NPR app,
or wherever you get your podcasts.

topics.text: Justice Department files third set of charges against former FBI Director James Comey
Judge orders Justice Department to reinstate fired prosecutor Maureen Comey with back pay
Mid-decade redistricting shifts 15 House districts, but few now look safe for Republicans
Anthropic files paperwork for initial public offering, possibly valuing firm at $1.5 trillion
S&P 500 rises 0.7 percent; earnings reports due this week from a third of stocks
French government pledges to replace national online university admissions platform in 2028
Maryland and Virginia school cafeterias serve invasive blue catfish to curb Chesapeake Bay predation
Five professional sports leagues have games scheduled on the same night
